subjectOf.text: The low transaction throughput of public blockchains is a core limitation holding back more advanced distributed applications and, with them, decentralized commerce.

subjectOf.text: The net and compress model used by post trade service providers exists because not every trade must be processed; on some estimates, processing every trade would require an additional 2.9 million orders per day.

subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Blockchain-Based Securities Offerings (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3411110

subjectOf.abstract: the expected growth rate illustrated in Figures [__] and [__] could mean that the Ethereum network will continue to experience network shortages and throughput issues unless the Ethereum infrastructure is upgraded to deal with the expected volume of transactions.

subjectOf.text: Decentralized banking addresses blockchain scaling, because the linear structure of a blockchain means that doubling the number of participants and transactions halves its speed.
subjectOf.abstract: Decentralized banking helps solve a major problem with blockchains called scaling. If you double the number of participants and transactions, the linear nature of the blockchain makes it slow down by half.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Finance (DeFi) (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782216

subjectOf.text: Working with suboptimal layer 1 blockchain solutions that carry high gas fees and low throughput delays the evolution of DAO infrastructure design, because innovation is inhibited by those layer 1 features.
subjectOf.abstract: Yet, working with suboptimal layer 1 blockchain solutions with high gas fees and low throughput delay the evolution of DAO infrastructure design as innovation and evolution is inhibited through suboptimal layer 1 features.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, A Decentralized Autonomous Organization (DAO) of DAOs (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3799320
scope_conditions: development anchored to first generation layer 1 networks

subjectOf.text: A truly decentralized public blockchain must satisfy three simultaneous requirements: no points of centralization and corruption, full security at the level of proof of work, and transaction throughput above one hundred thousand transactions per second.
subjectOf.abstract: That is, a public blockchain that is not subject to points of centralization and corruption, that is fully secure at the level of proof of work security with a transaction throughput of over one hundred thousand transactions per seconds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization – Why We Need Technology Infrastructure Upgrades (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808859
scope_conditions: stated as the requirement for technological decentralization via blockchain

subjectOf.text: Human-in-the-loop annotation, including under ethical labor models, imposes financial and time costs large enough to slow the pace at which AI models can be upgraded.
subjectOf.abstract: The reliance on human annotators, even with companies striving for ethical labor practices like CloudFactory, involves significant costs, both financial and in terms of time, which can slow down the pace of AI model upgrades.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Artificial Intelligence The Final Frontier (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5095633
scope_conditions: pipelines that depend on human annotators

subjectOf.text: Decentralized data annotation at scale is not operationally feasible without advances in consensus algorithms or layer-two scaling, because existing blockchain infrastructures cap transaction speed and network capacity.
subjectOf.abstract: existing blockchain infrastructures typically grapple with limits on transaction speed and network capacity. Continuous innovation in consensus algorithms, such as Proof of Stake or layer-two scaling solutions, is thus critical.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Artificial Intelligence The Final Frontier (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5095633
scope_conditions: real-time or near real-time annotation of large data volumes
